title: Finite prefix changes have an exactly computable global cost

plain_language.question: If the beginning of the target pattern changes, can its worst global matching penalty still be found exactly?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes. An explicit finite search finds the smallest additive allowance that works at every positive start, and a start inside the search attains it.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Certify the exact robustness cost for one specified finite prefix edit, not just use a universal overestimate.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: The theorem does not give a fast practical search or cover arbitrary edits indefinitely far along the sequence.

exact_statement_and_scope: Let m≥0 and let a binary target s agree with digit-parity Thue–Morse at every index k≥m, with no restrictions on its first m bits. Let L_s(v) be the attained maximum matching length in the original own-target BinaryAvoidance graph. Set N(m)=3·2^(m+3)+m and B_s=max_{1≤v≤N(m)}(3L_s(v)−8v), in the integers. Every positive v satisfies 3L_s(v)≤8v+B_s, some positive v≤N(m) attains equality, and an integer B is valid at every positive start iff B_s≤B. Also −1≤B_s≤8m−1. FiniteEditExact.height computes the needed maximum; FiniteEditOptimum.individual_optimum_attained and individual_additive_constant_iff supply the global finite-reduction endpoint.
